I really wanted to like this place, and I’m giving it 4 stars to support a new small business. That said, based purely on my experience, it was closer to a 2-star visit.

The restaurant itself is clean and nicely decorated, but there were several issues that made the experience disappointing. The air conditioning wasn’t keeping up, so the dining room felt quite warm. We also had an 8:30 PM reservation but weren’t seated until around 8:45 PM, and the staff seemed overwhelmed. Overall, the management felt inexperienced.

As for the food, the Lavashak Martini was excellent and easily my favorite thing we ordered. The Persian pizza was also very good.

The rest was underwhelming. Portions across the board were quite small for the price. The Tahchin was much smaller than expected, and the rosewater flavor was overpowering for my taste. The Kotlet was fairly basic and also on the small side.

The biggest disappointment was the Persian Macaroni. One of the reasons I ordered it was because the menu photo clearly shows a beautiful potato tahdig on top. What arrived looked completely different and had no potato tahdig at all. That felt misleading, especially since the photo was a major selling point. The macaroni itself wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t what was advertised.

I genuinely hope they succeed because it’s always nice to see new Persian restaurants open in NYC. With better consistency, more accurate presentation of the dishes, larger portions, and smoother service, I think this place has potential.

Overall, Cote was a great experience with excellent food and service. Pricey, yes, but worth it for a special night out.

location.address: 249 W 49th St, New York, NY 10019, United States

I had the mushroom pappardelle, which was fine but nothing special, and the zucchini spaghetti was about the same. It’s definitely a spot where the setting and drinks outshine the food. Still, it’s a fun place to hang out and enjoy the experience.

location.address: 36 St Marks Pl, New York, NY 10003, United States

The burrata slice wasn’t great though; it felt like a cheap version of the one from L’industrie. Still, the pizza overall was tasty and the atmosphere made it a fun spot to grab a few slices.

We went to Eyval for dinner and found parking without much trouble. The place had a nice energy with a modern look and a comfortable crowd.

The kitchen was fast and the food was excellent. The ghorme sabzi had deep flavor and tender meat. The tahdig was golden and crisp, and the kabob was juicy and well seasoned with saffron rice and grilled tomatoes.

The servers, however, weren’t very attentive. Drinks sat empty for a while, and it took some effort to get their attention. For two people, the total was about $120, which felt fair for the quality.

Overall, Eyval delivers top Persian food and a great vibe, but the service could be more engaged to match the kitchen’s pace.

location.address: 329 Van Brunt St, Brooklyn, NY 11231, United States

properties.review_text_published:
Red Hook Tavern feels like one of those neighborhood spots that’s been there forever. It’s warm and a little dim, with candles on the tables. Simple and comfortable.

We had a reservation, so we didn’t have to wait, but outdoor seating looked nice too, and the wait seemed around 30 minutes on a Tuesday night.

The burger was the reason we came, and it really was great. It’s dry-aged, so the flavor is strong and a little different, in a good way, but definitely something to know before you order. The potato chips were thick and fresh, the cheese was melted perfectly, and the pickle was honestly one of my favorite parts. I never thought I’d say that about a pickle, but it was that good.

It’s not a cheap meal, and you can tell part of what you’re paying for is the place’s reputation. The food’s solid, the space feels genuine, and the whole experience just fits together nicely.

location.address: 23 Godwin Ave, Ridgewood, NJ 07450, United States

properties.review_text_published: Kabob on the Cliff is a warm and welcoming spot with super nice staff who make you feel comfortable right away. The food is good and comes in generous portions, with the kabobs standing out as especially tender and flavorful, paired nicely with fluffy saffron rice. Other dishes like the stews are solid too. The vibe is relaxed and comfortable, making it a great place to enjoy a meal with friends or family. Overall, the quality ranges from moderate to good, but the friendly service and tasty kabobs make it a place worth visiting again.

location.address: 450 N Beverwyck Rd, Parsippany-Troy Hills, NJ 07054, United States

properties.review_text_published:
Reyhoon is a cozy, family-run spot that makes you feel welcome the moment you walk in. The service is warm and attentive, and the owner is kind and genuinely cares about the experience of his guests. The menu is excellent—there’s a wide range of authentic Persian dishes, from traditional stews to appetizers and kabobs, so you’ll have plenty to choose from.

The kabobs and rice are decent but could be improved. Since they’re such central parts of Persian cuisine, refining them would take this place to the next level. That said, everything else we tried was flavorful and clearly made with care.

I’m giving four stars not just for the food but also to support a hardworking family business that puts heart into what they do. With just a little more attention to the kabobs and rice, Reyhoon could easily become a standout Persian restaurant.

location.address: 173 Orchard St, New York, NY 10002, United States

Overall, the pizza is worth coming for. Just know there’s no bathroom for customers and no seating, so it’s more of a quick stop than a sit-down spot.

Emilio’s is a true community gem. It’s a family-run spot, and you can feel it right away – everyone in the family is working together, which adds a nice personal touch to the whole experience. There’s a warm, welcoming vibe that makes you want to come back.

The pizzas are very good, with a creative selection that goes beyond the usual options. They’re a little larger than your typical Neapolitan style, which means the crust edges can be tricky to pick up without flopping over – but the flavors and quality more than make up for it. The toppings are fresh, and the combinations are well thought out.

We also tried the meatballs, which were good. The meat was of good quality, and the sauce was rich and flavorful.

location.address: 1063 1st Ave, New York, NY 10022, United States
location.name: Au Za'atar - Midtown East

properties.review_text_published:
Au Za’atar looks inviting and the service was fine, but the experience left us disappointed. Shawarma is what they advertise most, so we assumed it was the highlight, only to find out after sitting down that it’s not even on the menu, something we wish we had known or at least been told to ask about.
Thinking the Mixed Grill Platter Supreme was the featured dish, we ordered it, but for nearly a hundred dollars it came out far smaller than described, nothing close to a meal for four. The baba ghanoush was tasty but tiny for the price, the bread was scarce, and the fries seemed like filler. Drinks were the final letdown; $6.50 for a Coke, felt excessive.
Overall, the food was fine, but between the missing shawarma, small portions, and steep prices, it didn’t feel worth it.

properties.review_text_published:
I ordered from Reza Persian Grill through Uber Eats. The food came well-packaged and neatly presented, which was a nice touch. The kabobs were excellent — juicy, flavorful, and cooked just right. The rice was fluffy and well-prepared.

The tahdig (crispy rice) was included, but it was a bit soggy by the time it arrived, which is understandable with delivery but still worth noting. I appreciated the extra touches like the fresh herbs (sabzi) and bread that came with the meal — it made the experience feel more complete and authentic.

Overall, the quality of the food was very good, and I would definitely order again, especially for the kabobs and rice. A solid option for Persian food in Houston.

Portions are huge, the kind where you laugh when it hits the table because you know you’re in for a challenge. The prices are surprisingly affordable for what you get, which makes it even better. The staff couldn’t be friendlier—warm, patient, and genuinely happy to see you enjoy yourself, which adds to the welcoming vibe of the place. The inside has this comfortable, small-town feel with hints of history in its décor and story, and you can sense that this creamery and farm house cafe has been around long enough to mean something to the community. Between the atmosphere, the people, the prices, and the quality, it’s one of those spots you end up wanting to come back to again and again.

location.address: 1141 Connecticut Ave NW, Washington, DC 20036, United States

properties.review_text_published:
Had lunch at Darvish and overall, it was a good experience. The atmosphere is calm and comfortable, and the place feels well-kept. Staff were friendly, and our waiter, Mohammad Reza, was great—super attentive and easy to talk to.

The food was solid, with some hits and a few things to keep in mind. The stews were definitely the best part—really flavorful and well-cooked. Kabobs were fine, not amazing, but still enjoyable. The rice was done well.

A couple of things to watch for: if you order koobideh or joojeh, they don’t come with rice. You’ll need to add $5 for that. Kind of annoying, especially since the stews do include rice. Also, Diet Coke was $6 with no refill, which felt overpriced.

All in all, it’s a nice spot with good food and great service. Just be aware of the menu quirks and pricing.

location.address: 80 Mamaroneck Ave, White Plains, NY 10601, United States
location.name: Shiraz Kitchen & Wine Bar

questions.question: Can you share more about these topics?

properties.review_text_published: It has a great atmosphere — the space is elegant, the vibe is relaxed, and the service is professional from start to finish. The staff were attentive without being overbearing, and the setting made for a comfortable dining experience. We started with the kashk-e bademjan, which was decent, enjoyable enough. The disappointment came with the main course: the kabobs. As someone who’s had kabobs across many Persian restaurants and knows what good ones taste like, I was genuinely surprised at how bland and low-quality they were. The meat lacked seasoning, depth, and tenderness, which made the beautiful presentation all the more frustrating. The biggest issue, though, is the price — Shiraz is shockingly expensive for what it offers, and while I understand paying more for ambiance and service, the food just doesn’t measure up. Overall, it’s a nice place to sit and be served, but if you’re looking for authentic, flavorful Persian cuisine, especially kabobs, this isn’t it.

On the other hand, the chicken tenders were actually really good — crispy, well-seasoned, and cooked just right. The lighting’s right, the music’s good, and it somehow feels like everyone there is in on the same relaxed, good-night-out mood. You leave full, happy, and already thinking about when you’ll be back.

location.address: 19 Old Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11201, United States

properties.review_text_published: On a sunny Sunday in Brooklyn, I waited about 30 minutes for a table at Juliana’s, and honestly, it was time well spent. The place runs like a well-oiled machine—super friendly staff, sharp service, and a warm, no-frills vibe that makes you feel like a regular even if it’s your first time. The coal-fired pizza is the clear standout, with a crisp, charred crust that nails the balance between chew and crunch, and while the dough and technique are top-notch, the ingredients could use a little upgrade to match the quality of the base. Still, Juliana’s delivers that rare mix of casual charm and serious flavor, making it a must-visit for any pizza lover in Brooklyn.

properties.review_text_published: Al Basha has a really warm, welcoming vibe—the decor is beautiful and sets the scene for what you hope will be a great meal. And to be fair, the food delivers. The meat was incredibly tender and clearly high quality, full of flavor and cooked just right. I also had the mint lemonade, which tasted a lot like a mojito—not what I expected, but still refreshing. The downside? It took exactly an hour to get our food, with no updates or apologies, which really tested our patience. On top of that, they automatically add an 18% tip to the bill, which feels a bit pushy, especially when the service is that slow.

location.address: 5061 Westheimer Rd Suite 8060, Houston, TX 77056, United States

The setting was sleek and comfortable—definitely a place that knows how to create a good dining mood. The staff was sharp, attentive without hovering, and everything ran smoothly from the moment I walked in.

The steak, though, just didn’t do it for me. It was dry and kind of forgettable, which was disappointing. Asparagus was the surprise standout—perfectly cooked with great flavor. Mashed potatoes were alright, nothing special. The chocolate mousse at the end made up for a lot—rich, not too sweet, and a nice finish. Glad I went, but I’d go for something other than the steak next time.

location.address: 1801 Post Oak Blvd Ste 120, Houston, TX 77056, United States
location.name: Rumi's Kitchen

Beautifully presented dishes and a warm, elegant atmosphere made for a pleasant dining experience. The space was clean, inviting, and clearly well-managed, with attentive staff who ensured great service throughout the meal. Everything ran smoothly and efficiently thanks to the strong team presence.

While the food was decent overall, the quality of the meat could be improved for a better culinary impact. Still, the visit was enjoyable and worth recommending for the overall ambiance and service.

location.address: 10 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023, United States

The vibe is vibrant and Afro-Caribbean—great music, stylish decor, and dishes that tell a story. Pricey ($241 for two with drinks), but it felt special.

Go for the food, stay for the atmosphere—and don’t skip the goat patties.

Both were nicely charred, thoughtfully balanced, and satisfying. The kind of pies you enjoy slowly, appreciating the craft behind them.

The space itself matched the food: relaxed, stylish, and welcoming without overdoing it.

All in all, a solid experience. We’d return without hesitation.

We also tried the Bufalina pizza, which was good but didn’t quite make a lasting impression. The restaurant was bustling, which slowed down the service a bit, but the vibrant atmosphere added to its charm. On a warm afternoon, the outdoor seating is a definite highlight, offering a more laid-back experience and a refreshing break from the indoor buzz. The portion sizes were just right, and despite a few minor hiccups, the overall experience was truly enjoyable.

location.address: 225 W 35th St A, New York, NY 10001, United States

If you’re looking for a quick bite and aren’t too picky, it might do the job, but for a place claiming to offer the “best,” expectations fall short.

properties.review_text_published: Au Cheval sits hidden in a rough little alley that might make you question your GPS, but step inside and it’s a whole different world—noisy, packed, chaotic in the best way, with a kind of charged energy that tells you people are here for something worth waiting for. We came for the burger, like everyone else, and while I wouldn’t call it the best I’ve ever had in terms of just the patty, that’s not really the point here—it’s the sum of everything stacked between that glossy bun that makes it shine: the gooey cheese, the crispy bacon, the runny farm egg that drips just enough, the soft-yet-sturdy bun holding it all together. Each bite felt like a messy, savory celebration, and the fries didn’t hurt either—crisp, hot, salty, perfect alongside the main event. The service held up surprisingly well given how slammed the place was, friendly and fast without rushing us. It’s loud, the kind of place where conversations compete with clanging plates and background chatter, but somehow it adds to the vibe rather than takes away from it. There’s something about the whole experience—the alley entrance, the energy, the indulgence of the burger—that makes it feel like more than just a meal, like you’ve joined some ongoing ritual of people hunting down one of the most talked-about burgers in town. Just don’t show up expecting peace and quiet or a quick seat—make a reservation, show up hungry, and be ready to dive into the chaos.

location.name: MORTON WILLIAMS SUPERMARKETS

properties.review_text_published: It is outrageously overpriced, with even the most basic groceries costing far more than they should. On top of that, the staff is consistently unprofessional, often inattentive, and at times even rude, making the shopping experience frustrating and unpleasant. It’s clear this store relies on convenience rather than offering fair value or decent customer service.

location.address: 226 Thompson St, New York, NY 10012, United States
location.name: Lava Shawarma NYC

properties.review_text_published:
Lava Shawarma offers a tasty beef and lamb shawarma—well-seasoned, tender, and satisfying. The garlic sauce was a bit too intense for my taste, but the overall quality of the food was solid. Staff were polite and service was smooth.

However, the ambiance was noticeably political, with strong pro-Palestinian messaging throughout the space. While political expression is understandable, some of the imagery and slogans gave off a tone that felt uncomfortably one-sided and, at times, veered into what could be interpreted as antisemitic. It made the dining experience feel more charged than welcoming. If you’re going just for the shawarma, it’s worth a visit, but the atmosphere may not sit well with everyone.

Tucked into a cozy spot, this place absolutely nailed the experience from start to finish. From the moment we sat down, the service was on point — friendly, attentive, and quick without feeling rushed. They packed our leftovers neatly and made sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal, checking in just enough to make us feel cared for without being intrusive.

The food was just as impressive. Generous portions arrived fresh and perfectly cooked. The kabobs were tender and full of flavor, and the saffron rice was incredibly fragrant and buttery. A standout was the charbroiled tomato — smoky, juicy, and easily one of the best I’ve ever had.

It’s rare to find a spot where everything just clicks like this. Five stars, without a doubt.

location.address: 189 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10012, United States
location.name: Figo il Gelato Italiano

properties.review_text_published: It has a friendly, welcoming staff that makes the visit pleasant, but the gelato itself is a mixed bag, especially considering the price—around $3 per scoop, which feels a bit steep for what you get. While the dark chocolate flavor stood out as rich and satisfying, other options didn’t quite hit the mark. The tiramisu was disappointing and lacked the expected depth, the lemon was overwhelmingly sour, and the Ferrero Rocher, while decent, didn’t offer anything memorable. Overall, it’s an okay spot, but I much prefer Venchi for both flavor and consistency—Figo earns a solid 3 stars.

location.name: Frank Pepe Pizzeria Napoletana

properties.review_text_published: Frank Pepe in Yonkers totally lived up to the hype. The coal oven crust was fantastic—crispy, a little charred in the best way, and full of flavor. We went on a weekend during prime time and had to wait about 15–30 minutes to be seated, but once we were in, the service was impressively fast. The atmosphere felt warm and authentic, and you can tell they use high-quality ingredients. You have the option to build your own pizza or choose from their specials. We tried the Caprese pizza and also made a custom one with meatballs, mushrooms, and black olives on a tomato and cheese base. The mozzarella was especially fresh and delicious. Overall, it was a really good experience—great crust, solid flavors, and a place I’d definitely return to.

location.address: 325 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10014, United States

properties.review_text_published: Tried Mama’s TOO! in the West Village and was pleasantly surprised — the novelty pizzas here are definitely worth checking out. The bruschetta slice was easily my favorite: fresh, bright, and full of flavor. The vodka slice was pretty good too, creamy and well-balanced, though not as memorable. I wasn’t a fan of the cacio e pepe slice — it felt like it was trying a bit too hard and didn’t quite land for me. That said, the staff were super nice, and the service was quick even with a bit of a line. Overall, a fun spot if you’re in the mood for something different.

location.address: 304 Washington St, Hoboken, NJ 07030, United States
location.name: Quality Pizza Co. Hoboken

properties.review_text_published: Quality Pizza in Hoboken is a solid spot for a quick, affordable slice. We tried the mushroom, margherita, and eggplant Sicilian—nothing mind-blowing, but all were good and hit the spot. It’s probably the best slice pizza we’ve had so far in the Hoboken and Jersey City area for the price. The place is fine overall—staff is professional, they give 10% off if you pay cash, and while the ambiance is okay and the cleanliness could be better, it does the job if you’re just looking for decent pizza without the fuss.

location.address: 30 Park Ln N, Jersey City, NJ 07310, United States
location.name: Efi's Gyro

properties.review_text_published:
Stopped by Elfi’s recently, and I’ve got to say—it’s a really lovely spot. The space is clean, nicely decorated, and has a warm, welcoming vibe that makes you want to stay a little longer.

What stood out most, though, was the staff. Everyone was super friendly and genuinely kind. You can tell they care about the place and the people who come in. That kind of hospitality makes a big difference.

The food? Solid. The presentation is clean and thoughtful, and the quality’s definitely there. It’s not over-the-top fancy, but it doesn’t need to be—it’s good, and it’s made with care.

If I had to nitpick, I’d say the portion sizes could be a bit more generous. Nothing major, just something that would make the overall experience even better.

All in all, Elfi’s is the kind of local business that deserves more love. Good food, great people, and a place that feels like part of the community. I’ll definitely be back.

The pizza, on the other hand, was the highlight—great crust with that perfect coal oven crisp, while the sauce and toppings were just okay, nothing that really stood out. The vibe of the place was warm and inviting, and the service was friendly and attentive, though it was a little annoying that drink refills only came if you asked for them. Overall, it felt like a solid neighborhood spot—good for a casual meal, especially if you’re craving pizza.

properties.review_text_published:
Saffron Bloom is one of those rare spots where you immediately feel the heart behind the operation. It’s a family-run place with a real person at the helm, and you can tell. The vibe is warm and welcoming—nothing flashy, just a comfortable, sincere atmosphere that makes you want to linger a little longer.

The staff are genuinely polite and friendly, and while they’re clearly juggling a lot (as both they and other guests have noted, they’re a bit understaffed), their attention and care really shine through. Be patient, and you’ll see how much effort they put into making guests feel at home.

As for the food—it’s solid with some room for growth. The saffron rice stood out, fragrant and perfectly cooked, and we were pleasantly surprised by a complimentary tahdig, which was a lovely gesture and much appreciated. The kabobs, while decent, could benefit from better meat selection or preparation—something that might improve as the place grows.

All in all, we’ll definitely be back. Supporting a local family business like this feels good, and with the kind of hospitality and vibe they offer, I’m hopeful that the food will continue to improve—especially the kabobs. Here’s to cheering them on as they fine-tune their craft.

properties.review_text_published: Ruth’s Chris Steak House delivers an upscale dining experience that feels both refined and welcoming, making it an ideal spot for a special occasion. From the moment you step inside, the dim lighting and candlelit tables set the stage for an intimate meal, while the staff’s professionalism ensures you’re well taken care of without feeling rushed. The real star of the night, though, is the steak—served sizzling on a hot plate, perfectly seasoned, and cooked to perfection. The ribeye arrives with a beautifully seared crust, locking in its rich, buttery flavor, while the filet is melt-in-your-mouth tender. The sides, like the creamy mashed potatoes, are comforting and well-executed, though they don’t steal the spotlight from the steak. A standout moment comes with the birthday dessert, a beautifully plated molten chocolate cake, complete with fresh strawberries and a raspberry drizzle, adding a thoughtful touch to the celebration. While the food and service live up to the reputation, the prices are on the high side, making it a place you visit for the experience rather than everyday dining. Still, for a night out that feels indulgent and special, Ruth’s Chris delivers on all fronts.

The restaurant feels more like a house than a typical dining space, which makes it warm and inviting, especially for a special occasion. The staff was great—attentive, friendly, and made sure we were taken care of without being overbearing. The food was okay, nothing bad but also nothing particularly memorable. It was well-prepared, but there wasn’t anything that stood out or made us feel like we’d come back just for the food. Pricing for the meal was fair, but the drinks felt overpriced compared to the rest of the experience. Overall, it’s a nice place if you’re looking for a relaxed, intimate dining setting with good service, but if you’re after an exceptional meal, it might not quite hit the mark.

The food at Toot Beirut is genuinely delicious—the spices on the shawarma and kabobs are perfect, and you can tell they know what they’re doing when it comes to flavor. Everything we tried was well-seasoned and tasted fresh.

But honestly, the portions are a joke. We ordered a platter for four, and there was no way it could actually feed four people. It felt more like a sampler than a meal. For the price, I expected a lot more food. Also, they don’t have fountain drinks, which isn’t a huge deal, but still kind of annoying.

The thing that really rubbed me the wrong way, though, was the pricing. They charge different prices for cash and card payments, which feels super sketchy. It’s one of those things that just leaves a bad impression and makes you not want to come back.

Overall, the food is great, but the portions and weird pricing policy make it hard to recommend.

I recently had dinner at The Capital Grille, and it was such a great experience. From the moment we walked in, the ambiance was warm and inviting—perfect for a special occasion or even just a nice night out.

Our server, TC, was fantastic. They were so attentive and friendly, making sure everything went smoothly and we had everything we needed. It’s rare to find service that’s both professional and genuinely personable, but TC nailed it.

One thing that stood out was how they made a birthday celebration feel extra special. They brought out a birthday card signed by the team and a delicious birthday cake, which was such a thoughtful touch. It made the night feel so personal and memorable.

Overall, everything about The Capital Grille was wonderful—great food, great atmosphere, and amazing service. I can’t wait to go back!

Additionally, the stews, particularly the ghormeh sabzi, lack the bold flavors typically expected, coming across as rather bland. On the bright side, the ambiance is pleasant, and the service is satisfactory, though the spiciness of the kabob was a bit too much for my personal preference. If authenticity is a priority, you might want to explore other options.

The decor is really nice and makes the whole space feel welcoming, and the big gift shop is a fun spot to browse after your meal. It’s a great place to visit if you’re looking for a good meal and a unique experience.

location.name: Peak with Priceless Restaurant & Bar

The ambiance is stunning, the service is excellent, and the food is absolutely fantastic—everything is beautifully prepared and full of flavor. That said, the portions are small, and the prices are very high, so be prepared to splurge. If you’re looking for a memorable dining experience with breathtaking scenery, this is the place to go.

The festive decorations and cozy ambiance made the entire place feel like a holiday dream, perfect for the occasion. The service was flawless—every staff member was attentive and welcoming, adding to the experience. The prix fixe menu was outstanding, with each course beautifully prepared and bursting with flavor. From start to finish, it was a magical evening, and I can’t imagine a better way to celebrate Christmas Eve.

location.address: 75 St Marks Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11217, United States
location.name: Sofreh

properties.review_text_published: Sofreh is a cozy spot with a lovely ambiance and authentic Persian food that goes beyond the usual kabobs. The dishes are thoughtfully prepared, full of rich flavors that feel both traditional and elevated. The staff are warm and welcoming, making the experience even more enjoyable. It’s a great place to explore Persian cuisine in a relaxed and inviting setting.

location.address: 113 Greenwich Ave, New York, NY 10014, United States
location.name: San Sabino

properties.review_text_published:
San Sabino is a gem that stands out with its delightful ambiance and creative take on Italian cuisine. From start to finish, the experience was nothing short of exceptional.

The dishes are incredibly innovative, showcasing a level of creativity and execution that’s rare to find. The quality of the ingredients is unmistakable, elevating every bite to something memorable.

The pasta? Simply one of the best I’ve ever had. Every strand and shape was perfectly cooked, and the flavors were bold yet balanced. The Octopus Carpaccio was a standout, offering a delicate yet flavorful start to the meal. As for the Manicotini Della Casa—it was nothing short of heavenly. Rich, decadent, and perfectly seasoned, it’s a dish I’ll be dreaming about for a long time.

San Sabino is a must-visit for anyone looking for a truly elevated Italian dining experience. I can’t wait to return!

location.address: 60 W 53rd St, New York, NY 10019, United States
location.name: Nusr-Et Steakhouse New York

properties.review_text_published:
If you’re seeking an extravagant dining experience with a hefty dose of sticker shock, Nusret New York might be the place for you. However, for us, it was an evening of high expectations and overwhelming disappointment.

To start, the pricing borders on absurd. A Diet Coke costs $9—and don’t expect a refill. The New York Strip, will set you back a staggering $77. Meanwhile, the burger, priced at $35, was utterly unremarkable and far from justifying its price tag.

Adding to the frustration, the service was pushy. Servers seemed more focused on upselling the most expensive menu items than ensuring a pleasant dining experience. Our reservation was at 7 PM, but we weren’t seated until 7:30, leaving us lingering for half an hour with no acknowledgment or apology.

By the end of the meal, we didn’t just feel overcharged—we felt insulted. For the exorbitant prices, one would at least expect exceptional service and food. Instead, Nusret left us questioning why we even bothered in the first place. Definitely not worth the hype or the cost.

The vibe inside has that same casual, welcoming energy, with a little New York edge. It’s busy, almost always crowded, but that’s just part of the experience. If you’ve ever craved a taste of In-N-Out while in the city, this place delivers with its own urban twist, making it a must-visit for burger lovers.

Still, it’s the kind of spot you try once for the history, the atmosphere, and that sauce you’ll be thinking about long after you’ve left.

location.address: 235 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10012, United States

properties.review_text_published: Rubirosa offers a lively dining experience with flavorful dishes that mostly hit the mark. The Tie-Dye Pizza was absolutely delicious, though the crust was a bit saggy. The Carbonara was rich and satisfying but had a bit too much garlic for my taste. The ambiance was warm and inviting, but the tables were crammed close together, making the space feel tight. Despite these minor issues, the overall experience was enjoyable, especially for the excellent pizza.

location.address: 205 E Houston St, New York, NY 10002, United States
location.name: Katz's Delicatessen

properties.review_text_published: Katz’s Deli is as authentic as it gets. The Reuben sandwich was perfection—juicy, tender pastrami piled high with melty Swiss, tangy sauerkraut, and just the right amount of dressing on perfectly toasted rye. As a meat lover, I was thoroughly impressed with their meat-based pizza, which was a delightful highlight of the evening.
